contract.words: Collect $6,000 of settled cash within 21 days using no up-front capital.

terms.proofCondition: $6,000 of settled cash received in the owner's account within 21 days

strategy.title: Fulfil the three signed playground-inspection purchase orders through PlaySafe Inspections
strategy.why: Three parks directors signed purchase orders at $2,400 each ($7,200, above the $6,000 target). PlaySafe quoted $900 per park system in writing, completes all three by day 10 and invoices net 60 (due day 70); the cities pay net 45 after the reports (day 55). Cash arrives before the supplier is paid, so no owner capital is advanced, and all $7,200 settles by day 55, inside the 75-day window.

alternatives.title: Look for further openings
alternatives.why: Not needed: the signed orders alone carry the target with $1,200 margin over it.

reviews.reasons: EXECUTABLE is the right stance: three WRITTEN_ACCEPTANCE agreements at $2,400 each (price fact is EVIDENCE: signed purchase orders dated 2026-11-20) from the payer itself, so price is this buyer's real purchase price and 3 x $2,400 = $7,200 >= $6,000 target. Fulfilment is the recorded fulfiller: PlaySafe Inspections (certified) quoted $900 per park system in writing, finishes by day 10; cost $2,700 total, well below price. Capital: cities pay net 45 after reports (day 10 + 45 = day 55); PlaySafe invoices net 60 from day 10 (day 70), so receipts precede the only spend; peak owner capital $0, inside the zero up-front limit. Ledger matches steps (3 receipts settling day 55, one spend day 70). Window: all $7,200 settles by day 55 < 75. After paying the supplier inside the window the account keeps $4,500; the objective is collected settled cash (not profit), and $7,200 is collected, so the target is met on its own terms. Owner hours: card says 1 human hour, no hours ceiling in the contract.

reviews.reasons: The contract window is now 21 days. NO_PLAN is right and the decisive gap is a true DEADLINE constraint: the only opening's signed POs (3 x $2,400 = $7,200) pay net 45 after the reports, PlaySafe finishes by day 10, so cash settles day 55 (card timeToFirstCash 55 days, EVIDENCE); even if the reports were delivered on day 0, net 45 lands on day 45, still after day 21, so $0 counts. Every other link stays established; Brain's SETTLES_IN_TIME is the only false link and matches decisiveLinks. The resolution is arithmetically right: the deadline must be at least day 55, or the cities must pay within 11 days of the day-10 reports (by day 21), in which case the supplier's net-60 invoice (day 70) still falls after the receipts and peak capital stays $0. It responds to my earlier findings correctly (moot under the new window).
findings: NOTE: Paying within 11 days changes the signed net-45 terms; nothing on the record says a municipal buyer will, so that branch is a request, not a plan, as the revision says.
